---
title: "Palmer Penguin Observations"
format:
  dashboard:
    orientation: rows
    scrolling: false
    theme:
      - cosmo
      - lolol.scss
      - lolol2.scss
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
library(palmerpenguins)

# Remove records missing the fields used in the dashboard.
penguins_clean <- penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(species), !is.na(island))

# Overall totals and the average share per species.
total_penguins <- nrow(penguins_clean)
total_species <- n_distinct(penguins_clean$species)
equal_share <- round(total_penguins / total_species, 1)

# Number of observations for each species.
species_summary <- penguins_clean |>
  count(species, name = "observations") |>
  arrange(desc(observations)) |>
  mutate(
    share = observations / sum(observations),
    label = paste0(
      comma(observations), " (",
      percent(share, accuracy = 0.1), ")"
    )
  )

# Total observations recorded on each island.
island_summary <- penguins_clean |>
  count(island, name = "observations") |>
  arrange(desc(observations)) |>
  mutate(
    share = observations / sum(observations),
    label = paste0(
      comma(observations), " (",
      percent(share, accuracy = 0.1), ")"
    )
  )

# Species composition within each island.
island_species <- penguins_clean |>
  count(island, species, name = "observations") |>
  left_join(
    island_summary |>
      select(island, island_total = observations),
    by = "island"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    share = observations / island_total,
    label = paste0(
      comma(observations), " (",
      percent(share, accuracy = 0.1), ")"
    ),
    island = factor(island, levels = rev(island_summary$island)),
    species = factor(species, levels = rev(species_summary$species))
  )

# Identify species observed on only one island.
exclusive_species <- penguins_clean |>
  distinct(species, island) |>
  count(species, name = "island_count") |>
  filter(island_count == 1) |>
  pull(species)

n_exclusive_species <- length(exclusive_species)

# Species rank variables for KPIs and Finding 1.
top_species_name          <- as.character(species_summary$species[1])
top_species_count         <- species_summary$observations[1]
top_species_share         <- species_summary$share[1]
top_species_percentage    <- percent(top_species_share, accuracy = 0.1)

second_species_name       <- as.character(species_summary$species[2])
second_species_count      <- species_summary$observations[2]
second_species_percentage <- percent(species_summary$share[2], accuracy = 0.1)

third_species_name        <- as.character(species_summary$species[3])
third_species_count       <- species_summary$observations[3]
third_species_percentage  <- percent(species_summary$share[3], accuracy = 0.1)

species_top_second_diff   <- top_species_count - second_species_count

# Island rank variables for KPIs and Finding 2.
top_island_name           <- as.character(island_summary$island[1])
top_island_count          <- island_summary$observations[1]
top_island_share          <- island_summary$share[1]
top_island_percentage     <- percent(top_island_share, accuracy = 0.1)

second_island_name        <- as.character(island_summary$island[2])
second_island_count       <- island_summary$observations[2]
second_island_percentage  <- percent(island_summary$share[2], accuracy = 0.1)

third_island_name         <- as.character(island_summary$island[3])
third_island_count        <- island_summary$observations[3]
third_island_percentage   <- percent(island_summary$share[3], accuracy = 0.1)

top_two_island_count      <- top_island_count + second_island_count
top_two_island_percentage <- percent(top_two_island_count / total_penguins, accuracy = 0.1)

# Helper function to render the finding cards in Row 3.
plot_finding_card <- function(eyebrow_text, body_text, accent_color, wrap_width = 100) {
  wrapped_body <- paste(strwrap(body_text, width = wrap_width), collapse = "\n")

  ggplot() +
    annotate(
      "segment",
      x = 0, xend = 0, y = 0.08, yend = 0.92,
      color = accent_color, linewidth = 2.2
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = 0.018, y = 0.84,
      label = toupper(eyebrow_text),
      hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
      size = 3.3, fontface = "bold", color = accent_color
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = 0.018, y = 0.58,
      label = wrapped_body,
      hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
      size = 3.4, lineheight = 1.28, color = "#1E293B"
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.005, 0.01))) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(4, 8, 4, 8)
    )
}

# Consistent colors across the visualizations.
species_colors <- c(
  "Adelie" = "#1E40AF",
  "Gentoo" = "#0D9488",
  "Chinstrap" = "#D97706"
)
```

#| label: species-chart
#| title: "Penguin Species Distribution"
#| expandable: false
#| fig-width: 7.0
#| fig-height: 4.0
#| fig-dpi: 300

ggplot(
  species_summary,
  aes(
    x = observations,
    y = reorder(species, observations),
    fill = species
  )
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = equal_share,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "#64748B",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    hjust = -0.08,
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#0F172A"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = equal_share,
    y = total_species + 0.45,
    label = paste0("Equal Share: ", equal_share),
    size = 3.1,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#475569"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.30))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste0(
      top_species_name,
      " Has the Highest Number of Observations"
    ),
    subtitle = "Total observations by species, compared with an equal share",
    x = "Number of Observations",
    y = "Penguin Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11.5) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      color = "#0F172A"
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      color = "#64748B",
      margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    axis.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      color = "#334155"
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      color = "#0F172A",
      size = 10.5
    ),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# Deep Analysis {scrolling="true"}

```{r}
#| label: stats-prep
#| include: false

# drop the 2 rows missing body measurements
peng_num <- penguins_clean |>
  filter(
    !is.na(body_mass_g),
    !is.na(flipper_length_mm),
    !is.na(bill_length_mm),
    !is.na(bill_depth_mm)
  )

avg_mass <- round(mean(peng_num$body_mass_g))
sd_mass <- round(sd(peng_num$body_mass_g))

# species summary stats
sp_stats <- peng_num |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g),
    sd_mass = sd(body_mass_g),
    med_mass = median(body_mass_g),
    iqr_mass = IQR(body_mass_g),
    min_mass = min(body_mass_g),
    max_mass = max(body_mass_g),
    mean_flip = mean(flipper_length_mm),
    sd_flip = sd(flipper_length_mm),
    mean_blen = mean(bill_length_mm),
    sd_blen = sd(bill_length_mm),
    mean_bdep = mean(bill_depth_mm),
    sd_bdep = sd(bill_depth_mm),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_mass))

# order boxplot x-axis from lightest to heaviest
mass_order <- rev(as.character(sp_stats$species))
peng_num <- peng_num |>
  mutate(sp_ord = factor(species, levels = mass_order))
sp_stats <- sp_stats |>
  mutate(
    sp_ord = factor(species, levels = mass_order),
    mean_lbl = paste0("Avg: ", comma(round(mean_mass)), " g")
  )

all_row <- peng_num |>
  summarise(
    Species = "Overall",
    n = n(),
    mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g),
    sd_mass = sd(body_mass_g),
    med_mass = median(body_mass_g),
    iqr_mass = IQR(body_mass_g),
    min_mass = min(body_mass_g),
    max_mass = max(body_mass_g),
    mean_flip = mean(flipper_length_mm),
    sd_flip = sd(flipper_length_mm),
    mean_blen = mean(bill_length_mm),
    sd_blen = sd(bill_length_mm),
    mean_bdep = mean(bill_depth_mm),
    sd_bdep = sd(bill_depth_mm)
  )

desc_tbl <- sp_stats |>
  mutate(Species = as.character(species)) |>
  select(-species, -sp_ord, -mean_lbl) |>
  bind_rows(all_row) |>
  mutate(
    n = comma(n),
    `Mass Mean ± SD (g)` = paste0(comma(round(mean_mass)), " ± ", comma(round(sd_mass))),
    `Mass Median (IQR)` = paste0(comma(round(med_mass)), " (", comma(round(iqr_mass)), ")"),
    `Mass Range (g)` = paste0(comma(round(min_mass)), "–", comma(round(max_mass))),
    `Flipper Mean ± SD (mm)` = paste0(number(mean_flip, accuracy = 0.1), " ± ", number(sd_flip, accuracy = 0.1)),
    `Bill Len Mean ± SD (mm)` = paste0(number(mean_blen, accuracy = 0.1), " ± ", number(sd_blen, accuracy = 0.1)),
    `Bill Dep Mean ± SD (mm)` = paste0(number(mean_bdep, accuracy = 0.1), " ± ", number(sd_bdep, accuracy = 0.1))
  ) |>
  select(
    Species, n,
    `Mass Mean ± SD (g)`, `Mass Median (IQR)`, `Mass Range (g)`,
    `Flipper Mean ± SD (mm)`, `Bill Len Mean ± SD (mm)`, `Bill Dep Mean ± SD (mm)`
  )

# chi-square, anova, correlation + linear fit
chi <- chisq.test(table(penguins_clean$species, penguins_clean$island))
chi_val <- round(unname(chi$statistic), 1)
chi_df <- unname(chi$parameter)
chi_p_txt <- ifelse(chi$p.value < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", round(chi$p.value, 3)))

fit_aov <- aov(body_mass_g ~ species, data = peng_num)
aov_res <- summary(fit_aov)[[1]]
f_val <- round(aov_res$`F value`[1], 1)
df1 <- aov_res$Df[1]
df2 <- aov_res$Df[2]
aov_p <- aov_res$`Pr(>F)`[1]
aov_p_txt <- ifelse(aov_p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", round(aov_p, 3)))

cor_res <- cor.test(peng_num$flipper_length_mm, peng_num$body_mass_g)
r_val <- round(unname(cor_res$estimate), 2)
r2_pct <- percent(unname(cor_res$estimate)^2, accuracy = 0.1)
cor_p_txt <- ifelse(cor_res$p.value < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", round(cor_res$p.value, 3)))

fit_lm <- lm(body_mass_g ~ flipper_length_mm, data = peng_num)
slope <- round(unname(coef(fit_lm)[2]), 1)

test_tbl <- data.frame(
  Test = c("Chi-Square", "One-Way ANOVA", "Pearson r & Linear Fit"),
  Variables = c("Species vs. Island", "Body Mass by Species", "Flipper Length vs. Mass"),
  Statistic = c(
    paste0("χ² = ", chi_val, " (df = ", chi_df, ")"),
    paste0("F = ", f_val, " (df = ", df1, ", ", df2, ")"),
    paste0("r = ", r_val, " (R² = ", r2_pct, ")")
  ),
  `p-value` = c(chi_p_txt, aov_p_txt, cor_p_txt),
  Result = c(
    ifelse(chi$p.value < 0.05, "Significant", "Not significant"),
    ifelse(aov_p < 0.05, "Significant", "Not significant"),
    ifelse(cor_res$p.value < 0.05, "Significant", "Not significant")
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-mass
#| title: "Body Mass by Species"
#| expandable: false
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 4.3
#| fig-dpi: 300

ggplot(peng_num, aes(x = sp_ord, y = body_mass_g, fill = species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = avg_mass, linetype = "dashed", color = "#64748B", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.52, alpha = 0.78, color = "#0F172A", outlier.color = "#475569", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(
    data = sp_stats,
    aes(x = sp_ord, y = mean_mass),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    shape = 23, size = 3.2, fill = "#FFFFFF", color = "#0F172A", stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = sp_stats,
    aes(x = sp_ord, y = max_mass + 220, label = mean_lbl),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.3, fontface = "bold", color = "#0F172A"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.14))) +
  labs(
    title = paste0(sp_stats$species[1], " Penguins Weigh the Most"),
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Overall avg: ", comma(avg_mass), " g (dashed) | ANOVA F(",
      df1, ", ", df2, ") = ", f_val, ", ", aov_p_txt
    ),
    x = "Species",
    y = "Body Mass (g)",
    caption = "Diamonds = mean (average)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11.5) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#0F172A"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#64748B", size = 9.5, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#64748B", size = 8.5, hjust = 0),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#334155"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#0F172A", size = 10.5),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

### Column {width=50%}

```{r}
#| label: plot-flipper
#| title: "Flipper Length vs. Body Mass"
#| expandable: false
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 4.3
#| fig-dpi: 300

ggplot(peng_num, aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.72, size = 2.2) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE,
    color = "#0F172A", fill = "#CBD5E1", linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = species_colors, name = "Species:") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Penguins with Longer Flippers Tend to Weigh More",
    subtitle = paste0("r = ", r_val, ", R² = ", r2_pct, ", ", cor_p_txt, " | about +", slope, " g per mm"),
    x = "Flipper Length (mm)",
    y = "Body Mass (g)",
    #caption = "Line shows the overall linear fit with a 95% confidence band."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11.5) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#0F172A"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#64748B", size = 9.5, margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#64748B", size = 8.5, hjust = 0),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#334155"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

### Column {width=46%}

::: {.card title="Interpretations" fill="false"}
- **Species and islands (Chi-Square):** Species and issland aren't independent across the `r comma(total_penguins)` penguins (χ² = `r chi_val`, df = `r chi_df`, `r chi_p_txt`). This almost tells us that where a penguin lives is where the same species lives.
- **Body mass across species (One-Way ANOVA):** Average weight differs significantly across the `r comma(nrow(peng_num))` measured penguins (F(`r df1`, `r df2`) = `r f_val`, `r aov_p_txt`). `r sp_stats$species[1]` is the heaviest (avg `r comma(round(sp_stats$mean_mass[1]))` g), while `r sp_stats$species[2]` (`r comma(round(sp_stats$mean_mass[2]))` g) and `r sp_stats$species[3]` (`r comma(round(sp_stats$mean_mass[3]))` g) are not that far in weight.
- **Flipper length and body mass (Correlation & Regression):** Flipper length and body mass have a strong positive correlation (r = `r r_val`, `r cor_p_txt`), that explains `r r2_pct` of the variation in body mass. Based on the linear regression, each 1 mm of flipper length adds `r slope` g of body mass.
:::
